claims.text: Conventionally processed refractory high-entropy alloys have a relatively homogeneous, coarse-grained microstructure.
The untreated coarse-grained alloy has high intrinsic strength.
The untreated coarse-grained alloy has limited ductility and nonuniform deformation.
The proposed intervention is approximately 30% cold reduction followed by annealing at 900–1100 °C for 10–30 minutes in an inert atmosphere.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will produce a bimodal structure containing fine recrystallized grains and retained coarse grains.
Pre-straining followed by short annealing promotes localized rather than complete recrystallization.
Short sub-transus annealing refines selected regions without causing complete grain growth.
Fine recrystallized grains enhance plastic-strain uniformity.
Retained coarse grains preserve high strength.
Retained coarse grains preserve impact-induced energy release.
The heterogeneous bimodal microstructure alleviates stress concentrations.
Alleviating stress concentrations delays crack initiation.
The treatment will increase tensile ductility relative to the untreated baseline.
The treatment will make plastic deformation more homogeneous relative to the untreated baseline.
The treatment will cause only minimal loss of strength.
The treatment will cause only minimal loss of impact-induced energy release.
Retained coarse grains act as sites of high energy absorption during impact.
Poor control of cold work, annealing temperature, or annealing duration can produce excessive refinement or grain growth and thereby reduce strength or impair impact performance.

contradictions.description: The target property is described as impact-induced energy release, but the mechanism invokes energy absorption and the experiment measures impact energy or energy absorption. Energy release and mechanical energy absorption are not interchangeable outcomes, so the decisive impact metric is internally inconsistent with the stated target.
